2026 Faculty · Six Speakers

People who teach
outside.

Every presenter at Field Notes Live was chosen because they work in the field — not just study it. You'll hear from naturalists, youth educators, researchers, land stewards, and program builders whose expertise comes from doing the work, often in difficult conditions.

All Speakers

Keynote Speaker
Maya Torres
Opening Keynote · Day Two
Director of Interpretation
Blue Ridge Conservancy
Keynote · Oct 19 · 9:00 am Main Hall

"Reading the Land: Integrating Climate Signals into Trail Interpretation"

Maya Torres has spent fifteen years training naturalists, park interpreters, and trail guides to read the landscape as a living dataset. Her approach bridges traditional ecological knowledge with phenological observation — teaching field educators to notice what's changed, what's shifting, and how to translate those signals for the public without tipping into doom.

In her keynote, Maya argues that the best climate communicators are people who know specific places intimately — the first wildflower on a particular slope, the timing of a particular bird's arrival — and that this kind of located, relational knowledge is exactly what formal climate education often lacks.

Before joining the Blue Ridge Conservancy, Maya led interpretive programs at Great Smoky Mountains National Park for eight years and has been published in the Journal of Interpretation Research and Outdoor Educator Quarterly.

Trail Interpretation Climate Communication Phenology Naturalist Training
Session Speakers · Day Two
Oct 19 · 10:00 am · Main Hall
Ben Okafor
Risk Management Specialist
Youth Outdoor Education Network
"Risk-Aware, Not Risk-Averse: Dynamic Safety Planning for Youth Groups"

Ben has developed risk management frameworks used by over 400 youth programs across 28 states. A former wilderness trip leader himself, he argues forcefully that overcautious liability policies do their own kind of harm by keeping young people — especially urban youth — out of wild places. His session presents a dynamic risk matrix that scales to trip type, age group, and environmental conditions.

Youth Programs Safety Planning Risk Assessment
Oct 19 · 11:00 am · Main Hall
Lila Chen
Program Director
Accessible Trails Alliance
"No One Left on the Trailhead: Building Truly Inclusive Outdoor Classrooms"

Lila designs programs that center the outdoor experience for participants who have historically been excluded — urban youth, people with physical disabilities, neurodivergent learners, and first-generation outdoor visitors. She founded the Accessible Trails Alliance's flagship Trailhead Fellows program, which has placed 120 inclusion specialists in parks across the Southeast.

Inclusion Accessibility Program Design
Oct 19 · 1:30 pm · Main Hall
Jordan Whitehorse
Land Relations Coordinator
Eastern Band Cherokee Nation
"Place-Based Learning Rooted in Indigenous Land Stewardship"

Jordan has spent 12 years developing educational partnerships between the Eastern Band Cherokee Nation and regional schools, parks, and outdoor programs. Her work centers the question that mainstream outdoor education often sidesteps: whose land is this, who has always known it, and how does that knowledge get passed on? She is candid about what non-Indigenous educators can learn from Indigenous land relationships — and what they cannot take.

Land Stewardship Place-Based Learning Indigenous Knowledge
Oct 19 · 2:30 pm · Main Hall
Dr. Sam Adeyemi
Environmental Psychology Researcher
Appalachian State University
"The Dose Makes the Medicine: Nature Exposure, Mental Health, and Youth Outcomes"

Dr. Adeyemi's lab at Appalachian State has spent a decade studying what kinds of outdoor experiences produce measurable psychological benefits for young people — and how long those benefits last. His session cuts through the hype to answer the question outdoor educators actually need answered: what can you honestly tell a parent, a principal, or a grant reviewer about why taking kids outside matters?

Mental Health Research Youth Outcomes
Workshop Presenter · Day One
Petra Novak
Workshop Presenter
Grants Director
Southern Appalachian Highlands Conservancy
Day One · Workshop A3 · 9:00 am · Conf. Room A

"Funding Your Programs: Grant Strategies for Outdoor Education"

Petra Novak has secured more than $8 million in grant funding for conservation and outdoor education programs over her career. Her workshop cuts through the mystification around grant writing — which funders to approach, how to write for non-specialists, and the most common mistakes that sink otherwise strong proposals.

Attendees leave with a customizable grant calendar template and a list of funders specifically interested in climate-responsive outdoor education. No prior grant writing experience required.
